decisions.question: How does the contract state the rejection of a DeepLink published to nav.resolved-intent that bus-api@v1 G40 now gives: as a clause of G1, as a new guarantee, or as reject lines alone?

options.label: extend G1 with a publish clause
options.consequence: No new id; the existing G1 reject library already covers G1, so the new lines are covered by its header; G1 reads as one invariant, no DeepLink after resolution, over this contract's declarations and the publish paths onto its resolved-intent topic.

options.label: new guarantee G28 with its own reject library
options.consequence: A separately restrictable id, but one invariant split across two ids, and a second reject library for the same misuse.

options.label: reject lines only, G1 text unchanged
options.consequence: The fixture would pin a rejection no guarantee states, and Refinement 9's old text scoping G1 to this contract's own declarations would contradict the fixture.

decisions.chosen: extend G1 with a publish clause
decisions.why: The step names it a G1 reject line, and G1 already states the invariant. Refinement 9 scoped G1 to this contract's own declarations only because bus-api@v1's publish then let the call compile; with G40 that reason is gone, so the scope widens to what G1 always meant. A separate id buys nothing here because reject sets run unrestricted at every producing gate (ADR-001 item 10). Signal that would have changed my mind: a phase needing to deliver or restrict the publish clause separately from the rest of G1.

decisions.question: Which publish paths does the new reject coverage exercise: the Publisher call S13 probed (P19), or both publish paths G40 types?

options.label: Publisher.publish only
options.consequence: One line, exactly S13's probe P19; Bus.publish's rejection would be stated in G1 but unpinned.

options.label: both Bus.publish and Publisher.publish
options.consequence: Two lines; every path G1's clause names is pinned; the Bus.publish line needed its own confirmation (probe Q02).

decisions.why: G40 types both and G1's clause names both, so a fixture for one leaves half the clause unpinned. Q02 shows Bus.publish reports could_not_infer alone, like the Publisher line. They live in the existing G1 library rather than a new one, because ADR-001 item 4 groups reject fixtures per guarantee or per misuse, and this is the same misuse (a DeepLink where a resolved intent is required).

decisions.question: Refinement 8: keep this contract's own reading of bus-api@v1 G22 and G34 and add citations, or replace the reading with what G22 and G34 now state?

options.label: keep the reading, add citations
options.consequence: Two texts of the same rule, this contract's reading and bus-api@v1's guarantees, which can drift; the note that bus-api@v1's fixtures do not pin it would be false and would have to go anyway.

options.label: cite G22 and G34 as stated, history to Versioning
options.consequence: One definition, owned by bus-api@v1; Refinement 8 keeps why G14 and G24 depend on it and the evidence that a runtime without it drops a deep link; the history moves to the Versioning touch line.

decisions.chosen: cite G22 and G34 as stated, history to Versioning
decisions.why: Read side by side, bus-api@v1 G22 (connection before activate returns; connection-caused publishes from a provider-zone microtask) and G34 (every topology activated before start() connected when start() delivers the queue, even with nothing run between; the queue reaching those reads in its order) state the reading clause for clause. A second definition is the fork the skill warns against. G14 and G24 now cite G22 and G34 directly, and G24's 'as Refinement 8 reads them' became '(Refinement 8)'. Signal that would have changed my mind: any clause of the old reading that G22 or G34 did not state.

decisions.question: Refinement 9: does the contract say that explicit type arguments still let a DeepLink onto nav.resolved-intent, or leave it implicit in 'with its type arguments inferred'?

options.label: state the residual
options.consequence: One sentence and a probe line (Q08); G1's 'impossible by construction' is not over-read; matches G40's own residual sentence.

options.label: leave it implicit
options.consequence: Shorter, but a reader of G1 could take the publish clause to cover publish<NavIntent, DeepLink>, which compiles.

decisions.why: G40 states the same residual for its own guarantee, and Q08 confirms publish<NavIntent, DeepLink>(NavigationTopics.resolvedIntent, DeepLink(uri)) compiles on the stand-in. Refinement 9 keeps the earlier TypeError history, which bus-api@v1's Versioning cites as 'navigation-api@v1 Refinement 9', so that cross-reference stays true.

decisions.question: The Validation bullet on the Flutter binding of the executor suite: name the file flutter-binding@v1 wrote only, or also the order in which its executor constructs and pumps?

options.label: path only
options.consequence: Least duplication with flutter-binding@v1's Validation; the harness description here stays silent on an order the real binding fixes.

options.label: path and construct-before-pump order
options.consequence: One more clause repeated from flutter-binding@v1's Validation (drift risk if that binding changes), but this contract's description of what the binding supplies matches the file it names.

decisions.why: S14 records that flutter-binding@v1's binding constructs the executor before pumping its WidgetsApp, where the stand-in binding of S12 pumped first, and that both orders pass. The bullet already repeated the binding's settle and elapse; adding the order keeps it accurate to the named file at the cost of one clause. The stand-in sentence in the last Validation bullet now says the named binding replaces it. Close call: if flutter-binding@v1's binding were expected to change its order, path only would be the better choice.

decisions.question: Is the touch compatible within v1, or does G1's new clause make it breaking?

options.label: compatible within v1
options.consequence: Version kept; a Versioning line records the touch; consumers change nothing.

options.label: breaking, draft v2
options.consequence: A migration note and a second version for a clause that rejects nothing bus-api@v1 does not already reject.

options.label: run-stop-candidate
options.consequence: Only if an existing fixture or consumer fixture failed against the amended stand-in.

decisions.why: No declaration changed, no guarantee was removed or weakened, no id moved. The clause adds no rejection of its own: bus-api@v1 G40 already rejects the call, so no code that compiled after S13 stops compiling, which is this contract's Versioning rule for a compatible change (a new guarantee that existing fixtures still pass). The fixtures at 6843dc2, the amended fixtures, and flutter-binding@v1's executor binding all pass against the stand-in (B.1 to B.5, A.1 to A.5); the fixture diff is the one reject file (T2). Taken after the first full run of the experiment.

experiments.question: Does the new G1 reject coverage report the expected codes against a stand-in that meets bus-api@v1 as amended, do navigation-api@v1's fixtures as they stood before the touch still pass against it, and is flutter-binding@v1's binding of the executor suite unaffected?
experiments.finding: On the stand-in packages of flutter-binding-fixtures, unchanged (T0; runtime and navigation those of bus-api-amendment, typed publish on both paths): pages.publish and bus.publish of DeepLink(uri) to nav.resolved-intent each report could_not_infer alone, as does a NavIntent-typed value; resolved intents, nav.intent publishes, explicit type arguments publish<NavIntent, DeepLink> and the pre-amendment form compile (T1 Q01 to Q09). The fixtures differ only in reject/resolved_intent_is_never_a_deep_link.dart (T2). Before (6843dc2) and after alike: structure for navigation-api (27 guarantees, 66 cases, 2 bindings) and flutter-binding (19, 52, 2) passes, surface clean, every reject code confirmed, the navigation suite 40/40, the executor suite 52/52 on InMemoryRouter, flutter_navigation_executor_test.dart 26/26 under fvm flutter test --no-pub. The amended ADR-001 structure prototype passes all nine contracts (T3). With both publish signatures reverted to publish<T>(MultiWriterTopic<T>, T), the amended reject set fails on that file alone (the two could_not_infer lines vanish) while the before-touch reject set passes, so the new lines are what pins G40 for this topic (T4).
